newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela govt won't rescue Viasa from bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela govt won't rescue Viasa from bankruptcy.

text.p: The Venezuelan government will not inject any more funds into struggling international carrier Viasa, meaning the airline appears to be headed for bankruptcy, a top government official said Friday.

"The destiny of the company is liquidation or bankruptcy because we cannot continue injecting more money (into it)," deputy Planning Minister Armando Leon told reporters after a meeting of government ministers analyzed Viasa's future.
Audits have shown that the company, 45 percent owned by Spain's Iberia since 1991, has debts of more than $150 million.
"Viasa's financial situation is worse than was originally thought," Leon said.
"It is inevitable due to the amount of costs and debts which it has and any amount of money that is injected goes into a bottomless pit," he added.
The Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) -- the government body in charge of privatization -- owns 40 percent of the airline.

Iberia and the FIV agreed on a plan to rescue the airline in Madrid last month. But the proposal, which would involve job cuts and a fresh injection of capital, has not yet been approved by shareholders or by the airline's 2,250 workers.
Viasa suspended all flights Jan. 23 after workers rejected a previous restructuring plan.
Comapny sources have said shareholders were due to meet to discuss the airline's future Feb. 20.
